title: Addressing the Silent Soil Health Crisis
description: This editorial is based on “Soil health on the decline” published in The Hindu Business Line on 17/06/2026. The article emphasises that record food production masks a critical crisis of soil degradation. It advocates for restorative, ecosystem-based management to safeguard soil productivity, climate resilience, and public health across the nation. For Prelims: Soil Health Card (SHC) Scheme, Soil Organic Carbon, Heatwave, State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World 2025, UNCCD, Land Degradation Neutrality, Green Revolution, Heavy Metals, Mulching, Bio-fertilizers, Agroforestry. For Mains: Role of soil in long-term viability of Indian agriculture, reasons behind depletion of soil health and steps needed to restore soil health. India has achieved a record foodgrain harvest of 354 million tonnes in 2024-25. However, this quantitative success masks a deepening dual crisis of human malnutrition and deteriorating soil biological health, which threatens the long-term sustainability of its agricultural model. It demands a shift toward regenerative practices. For this, integrating soil-centric policies with precision technology is vital to ensure long-term agricultural sustainability and national nutritional security.
